authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Curated UI (the widget schema w = ⟨inputs, render, emits⟩, inputs ⊆ dim(S), emits ⊆ T); §II's typed-edit discipline for the two-containment shape
note: ★★ The row's property is not *there is a checker* — it is *the check is ON the load path*. A widget that does not typecheck must be **unable to reach a surface**, structurally, rather than merely checkable by whoever remembers to call the checker.

★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile_AND_THE_CRUX_WAS.1_there_is_NO_widget_code_in_this_core_a: ★★ Checked before designing, and it decided the slice: `curated` is **grep-0** in `sustena-core/src`, and every `widget` / `Widget` / `salience` hit is **prose in a doc comment** — `editing.rs` explaining why `RebindWidget` is absent, `monitor.rs` naming `WidgetVisualEncoder` as a row, `region.rs` saying its distance is the salience quantity, and MON-7's own header. **No widget type, no binding table, no `compose(r)`, no knapsack, no load path.**
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile_AND_THE_CRUX_WAS.★★_2_so_the_honest_scope_is_BUILD_THE_LO: Porting `validate_widget_schema` here would have produced a checker **beside nothing**, which checks nothing and cannot have the property the row is about. The row is the typed load path itself, with the judgment on it — which is also why the fix is cheap: there is no existing untyped path to retrofit, so the check can be structural from the first line rather than bolted onto a surface that already loads widgets without it.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile_AND_THE_CRUX_WAS.★_3_the_substrate_it_reads_ALREADY_EXIST: `dim(S)` is `Definition.schema` and `T` is `Definition.operators` — the same two things EDIT-13's `π` walks. Inputs are parsed with `predicate::parse_state_path`, which exists **precisely so a second wildcard-path grammar does not appear inside this crate** (its own docstring says so, citing the Constraint article's record of the reference's two divergent evaluators). Wildcards work because `Schema::declares` already handles them.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile_AND_THE_CRUX_WAS.★★_4_AND_STEP_0_CAUGHT_THIS_REPOSITORY_O: ★★★ MON-7's vector, written yesterday, recorded *urgency → selection* as **`AT PARITY — curated_ui.py's knapsack there, curated_ui.rs's equivalent here`**. There is **no `curated_ui.rs`**. The line was wrong, it was written by this same process one slice earlier, and it is **corrected in that vector rather than quietly left standing** — a vector that overstates parity is the single failure mode this whole discipline exists to catch, and it is worth recording that the discipline caught one of its own.

divergence.statement: The reference has `validate_widget_schema()` and it is **off the load path** (R2 #25). The check exists and is real; nothing on the path from a declared widget to a rendered one is obliged to call it. So a widget naming a made-up dimension or an unregistered operator loads, renders, and fails later — or worse, silently no-ops.
divergence.★★_the_counterweight_THE_CHECK_ITSELF_IS: ★★ The judgment this row enforces was **written there first**. `w = ⟨inputs, render, emits⟩` with `inputs ⊆ dim(S)` and `emits ⊆ T` is the reference's own schema and its own check — this core did not invent the shape, the containments or the idea of typing a widget against the definition. ★ And the Curated UI module as a whole is **mostly built** there, which the article's own headline correction records: typed widgets, β keyed on event class, `compose(r)` as a pure computed value, a genuine knapsack and deterministic effect-first capture all ship in Python. ★★ So the gap is **one word wide** — *on* — and that is the honest size of it: not *the check does not exist*, but *nothing makes it run*. The same shape `min_privilege`, `Skin` and `colour_rule` all had before their rows closed, and naming it as a pattern rather than an oversight is what makes it a class of defect rather than four accidents.

divergence.the_honest_limits: ★★ THIS IS THE LOAD PATH, NOT A SURFACE — a `LoadedWidget` carries a checked declaration and an opaque `render` tag; nothing here draws, lays out, or decides what to show. `compose(r)`, the binding table β and the knapsack are later UI rows, and MON-7 already drew the same encoder/renderer line for the same reason: this core has no display. · ★★ `render` IS AN OPAQUE STRING, DELIBERATELY — typing it would mean inventing a card/ring/feed vocabulary here, which is the core acquiring an opinion about rendering. The cost is real and stated: a misspelled render tag is **not** caught at load, because the core has nothing to check it against. That is a surface-side check, and pretending otherwise would be the same off-the-load-path defect one layer over. · ★★ THE PARAMS OF AN EMISSION ARE NOT TYPE-CHECKED — `emits ⊆ T` says the operator exists and is permitted; it does not say the params match its signature. `OperatorMeta` has no params schema in this core (IMM-10's `build_params` reaches for `inspect.signature` on the Python side precisely because of that), so a params check would need a mechanism that does not exist. The gate still catches it at execution; the point is it is caught **there** and not here. · ★ A LOADED SET CAN GO STALE, AND SAYS SO BUT DOES NOT SELF-HEAL — a typed `Edit` retiring a dimension or an operator invalidates the set. `is_current_for` detects it against a key over `dim(S)` and `T` only (an invariant change is deliberately not staleness, since a widget check does not depend on invariants), but nothing reloads automatically; the host does. · ★ ALL-OR-NOTHING IS A POSITION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT — a partial load is silent degradation, and a surface that quietly renders four cards instead of five cannot be debugged by the person looking at it. · AND NOTHING WIRES A `WidgetEmission` TO `execute` HERE — the emission is a typed request the host runs through the gate, the same seam every other core→host boundary uses.

load_path_cases.name: a_valid_widget_loads
load_path_cases.why: The positive case, first: a widget whose inputs are declared dimensions and whose emits are permitted, registered operators loads and is retrievable by id. A check that only ever refuses is not a type-checker, it is a wall.
load_path_cases.expect: Ok(WidgetSet) with the widget present, render tag and inputs intact

load_path_cases.name: ★★_a_made_up_input_is_rejected_AT_LOAD
load_path_cases.why: ★★ `inputs ⊆ dim(S)`, enforced where it matters. A typo'd dimension (`finaces.liquid` for `finances.liquid`) does not produce a widget that renders blank or reads `null` at runtime — it produces **no widget at all**, with the widget and the path both named. This is the row's headline behaviour and the reason the check being on the path is the property rather than the check existing.

load_path_cases.name: ★★_an_unpermitted_emit_is_rejected_AT_LOAD
load_path_cases.why: ★★ `emits ⊆ T`. `budget.spend` **is** registered — the definition simply does not list it — so exactly one error fires and it is the right one. A widget cannot even name an operator this sustain does not permit, which means the operator allow-list bounds the surface and not only the gate.

load_path_cases.name: ★_an_unregistered_emit_is_a_DIFFERENT_error_from_an_unpermitted_one
load_path_cases.why: ★ *This sustain does not allow it* and *it does not exist* send an author to different repairs — add it to the definition, versus write the operator. Kept apart for the same reason EVT-15 splits `Refused` from `NotPermitted` and IMM-7 splits `NoEdge` from `InsufficientTier`. Proven by a definition that **does** permit an operator nothing registers, so only the registry error fires.
load_path_cases.expect: Err containing NotRegistered and no NotPermitted

load_path_cases.name: an_unparseable_input_is_reported_as_such
load_path_cases.why: A third distinct finding: *that is not a path* is not the same as *that path names nothing*. Reusing `predicate::parse_state_path` means the widget layer and the predicate layer agree about what a path even is, which is the point of that function existing.

load_path_cases.name: a_wildcard_input_is_accepted_where_the_schema_declares_the_map
load_path_cases.why: `pockets[*]` against a declared `Map` type loads, because `Schema::declares` already understands that a wildcard steps into an open map. Reuse rather than a second grammar — the widget layer inherits the schema's own idea of what is declared.

structural_cases.name: ★★★_every_error_is_reported_not_only_the_first
structural_cases.why: ★★ Three defects in one widget produce three errors, not one. Fixing a surface one message at a time is exactly the experience `editing::typecheck`'s *well-typedness is a property of the whole definition* already avoids, and a load path that stops at the first problem trains an author to run it repeatedly rather than read it once.
structural_cases.expect: three errors from a widget with two bad inputs and one bad emit

structural_cases.name: ★★_one_bad_widget_refuses_the_WHOLE_set
structural_cases.why: ★★ A deliberate position, not an oversight. A partial load — keep the good widgets, drop the bad — is **silent degradation**: the widget simply is not there, which is indistinguishable from one that decided it had nothing to show. A surface that fails loudly can be fixed; one that quietly renders four cards instead of five cannot be debugged by the person looking at it. Fail-closed, IMM-4's rule at the surface.
structural_cases.expect: a valid widget and a broken one together yield Err

structural_cases.name: a_duplicate_id_is_refused
structural_cases.why: Two widgets sharing an id makes every later reference ambiguous — including the emission's own `widget_id`, which is how a host attributes a request back to what asked for it.

containment_cases.name: a_loaded_widget_may_emit_what_it_declared
containment_cases.why: The positive half of the inner containment, and it carries the widget id so a host can attribute the request. An emission has no public constructor either — the only source is `LoadedWidget::emit` — so a request naming an operator no widget declared cannot be forged and handed to the gate.

containment_cases.name: ★★_a_loaded_widget_may_NOT_emit_what_it_did_not_declare
containment_cases.why: ★★ The inner containment, and the case that shows the two are genuinely nested rather than one check twice. `budget.record_income` **is** permitted by the definition — this widget just never asked for it — so the load-time check passed and the emit-time check still refuses. A widget's authority is bounded by its own declaration *and* by the definition, the same shape IMM-10 gives a learned rule with its ingress bound.

containment_cases.name: params_travel_with_the_emission
containment_cases.why: The emission is a complete typed request the host can run through the gate — operator, params, and the widget that asked. Params are carried, not checked: see the limits on why a params type-check needs a mechanism this core does not have.

containment_cases.name: ★_retiring_a_dimension_makes_a_loaded_set_STALE
containment_cases.why: ★ EDIT-13 just made definition edits real, so a loaded surface can now be invalidated by one. A set knows the `dim(S)`/`T` it was checked against and can **say** it has gone stale rather than rendering against a definition that no longer holds. It does not self-heal — the host reloads — and that boundary is named rather than assumed.

containment_cases.name: ★_changing_an_invariant_does_NOT_make_a_set_stale
containment_cases.why: ★ The staleness key covers `dim(S)` and `T` **only**, because a widget check depends on nothing else. A key over the whole definition would report staleness that is not there and send a host reloading its whole surface every time a rule was tightened — a false alarm is a cost, not a safe default.
